crude.up_what: Importer currencies tend to weaken against the dollar, and exporter currencies tend to firm.
crude.up_view: Check unhedged import-currency payables, and whether current hedge cover still matches the next payment cycle.
crude.down_what: Importer currencies tend to firm against the dollar, and exporter currencies tend to ease.
crude.down_view: Do not unwind hedges on a single price move; test hedge ratios against the updated forecast first.

crude.up_what: Higher crude lifts headline inflation, which can keep central banks tighter for longer.
crude.up_view: Run floating-rate interest cost scenarios on a higher-for-longer path before the next central-bank decisions.
crude.down_what: Lower crude eases headline inflation and can give central banks room to pause.
crude.down_view: Check that fixed-rate issuance plans still stand; one price move is not a policy signal.

crude.up_what: Fuel and input costs rise, so cash tied up in inventory and receivables grows.
crude.up_view: Confirm committed credit lines cover the larger working-capital swing, and what it costs at current short-term rates.
crude.down_what: Working-capital needs ease, and released cash sits in short-term deposits.
crude.down_view: Refresh the cash forecast, then apply the investment policy's tenor and counterparty limits to any released cash.

crude.up_what: Commodity hedges settle daily, so on positions that lose when prices rise, a sharp move can call for cash within a day.
crude.up_view: Check the cash buffer held for variation margin, and who can approve a same-day transfer.
crude.down_what: On positions that lose when prices fall, the margin call comes on the way down instead.
crude.down_view: Check which hedges lose value on a fall, and that the buffer and same-day approval route still suffice.

crude.up_what: Energy-heavy customers and suppliers come under pressure, while producers' credit tends to improve.
crude.up_view: Re-rank counterparty exposure by energy sensitivity, and review limits where payment terms are long.
crude.down_what: Producers come under pressure, while energy-heavy users get relief.
crude.down_view: Re-rank counterparty exposure for producers, and review limits where payment terms are long.

points.head: Qatar money markets
points.text: QCB raised its deposit, repo and lending rates by 25 bp each from 17 September, to 4.10%, 4.35% and 4.60%. The deposit rate now sits above both SOFR (3.88%) and the top of the Fed range (4.00%), with the riyal pegged at QAR 3.64 per USD.
points.view: Compare riyal deposit yields with dollar alternatives for the same tenor before placing surplus cash, and keep counterparty limits fixed while yields rise.
points.s2n: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
points.title: The QCB deposit rate of 4.10% now sits above SOFR and the top of the Fed range

points.head: Qatar equities
points.text: The QE Index closed at 9,209.53 on 7 October, with QR 200.7mn traded and a market capitalisation of QR 558.7bn.
points.view: Value any listed holdings at the reporting-date close and keep them out of cash equivalents; a single day's close is not a reason to change the investment policy.
